scenes.title: The Arbitrage Tug-of-War: Spot-Futures Convergence
scenes.badge: HYPOTHETICAL DESK EXAMPLE · LAW OF ONE PRICE

beats.en_subtitle: When futures exceed spot at maturity, arbitrageurs sell futures, buy spot, and deliver for profit.

semantics.teachingObjective: Illustrate spot-futures convergence pressure using hypothetical desk pricing example

beats.en_narration: What guarantees that paper futures prices reflect real cash asset values? The answer is delivery arbitrage. If futures trade above the spot price at maturity, arbitrageurs sell futures, buy spot, and deliver for profit.

beats.en_subtitle: When futures trade below spot, buyers scoop up cheap futures contracts and demand delivery.

bottomPill.text: Buyers buy cheap futures to stand for delivery
Buyers buy cheap futures to stand for delivery

semantics.teachingObjective: Illustrate spot-futures convergence pressure using hypothetical desk pricing example

beats.en_narration: Conversely, if futures trade below the spot price, traders buy the undervalued futures contracts, take delivery at maturity, and sell the underlying asset in the cash spot market.

beats.en_subtitle: This arbitrage pressure pulls both prices into balance, forcing futures to equal spot at expiry.

bottomPill.text: Delivery arbitrage eliminates any pricing gap
Delivery arbitrage eliminates any pricing gap

semantics.teachingObjective: Illustrate spot-futures convergence pressure using hypothetical desk pricing example

beats.en_narration: This dual arbitrage pressure continually pulls both prices together, guaranteeing that the futures price mathematically converges to the spot price on expiration day.
